pageCache.pageTitle: Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Our Vision
The Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary School
Jesus said, “I have come in order that you might have life—life in all its fullness.” (John 10:10). This is the precept upon which Rochester Riverside is founded. We are committed to enabling each member of our community to flourish. With the role model of Christ as our cornerstone, we are building together a new community - a bridge from our past to the future.
Our vision defines all that we do, both within our school community and beyond.
Welcome to Rochester Riverside Primary School!
It is a real pleasure to welcome you to our school community—a place where everyone is known, valued, and encouraged to flourish. I am incredibly proud of our school and the caring, supportive environment we create together each day.
At the heart of everything we do is our vision, inspired by the words of Jesus: “I have come in order that you might have life—life in all its fullness” (John 10:10). We live this out by helping every member of our community discover their unique gifts and embrace every opportunity to grow.
Our school, like our children, is always growing and developing, and we are committed to building strong foundations for the future. With Christ as our cornerstone, we nurture a safe, happy, and inspiring environment where children are encouraged to reach their full potential. We are proud to be “bridge-builders”—connecting our past with our future, and working in close partnership with families and the wider community.
We believe school should be a place filled with joy, curiosity, and discovery. Our aim is to nurture not only confident and successful learners, but also happy, well-rounded individuals with a lifelong love of learning.
This vision comes to life through our “Forever Five” attributes: Compassion: Trustworthiness: Respect: Aspiration: Thankfulness:
These attributes are woven through everything we do—learning, play, and worship—and support our children long beyond their time with us. Together, we help every child grow with confidence, ready for the journey ahead, and proud to be Forever Riverside.
Mr Taylor (Headteacher)
The school is grateful for the ongoing support for our pastoral care provision from Hyde Charitable Trust.

pageCache.pageTitle: Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary School - PSHE including RSE
pageCache.text:
PSHE including RSE
In our school, we believe relationships lie at the very heart of what it means to be human. We believe we are created in the image of God; a God who is love,
“We love because He first loved us.” 1 John 4:19
Loving relationships enable us all to flourish. Rochester Riverside PSHE and RSE Policies are written to reflect our school vision:
Jesus said, “I have come in order that you might have life—life in all its fullness.” (John 10:10)
This is the precept upon which Rochester Riverside is founded. We are committed to enabling each member of our community to flourish.
With the role model of Christ as our cornerstone, we are building together a new community - a bridge from our past to the future.
Intent
Curriculum Intent in PSHE:
In Rochester Riverside we aim to support pupils to:
Promote Christian values.
Develop respect for others.
Develop a healthy and safe lifestyle.
Be aware of safety issues.
Actively promote British Values.
Curriculum Intent in RSE:
In Rochester Riverside we believe:
Implementation
The ‘Pilgrim Progress’ is a bespoke series of documents which forms the backbone of our own curriculum, ensuring implementation of appropriate subject coverage and expectation, whilst allowing for personalisation particular to our Pilgrim children.
Visitors to our School
At Rochester Riverside, we were lucky enough to be visited by a Fire Safety Officer. He came to our school to tell us more about how we can keep ourselves safe in our homes. We learnt a very important rhyme, "MATCHES AND LIGHTERS, NEVER TOUCH, THEY CAN HURT YOU VERY MUCH!" The Fire Safety Officer then went on to explain the importance of smoke alarms in our homes and told us that we need to check them at least once a week. We decided that Tuesdays would be a great day to test our smoke alarms and we could call it, "Test it Tuesday!"

pageCache.pageTitle: Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
At Rochester Riverside School, we aim to make music a fun and worthwhile learning experience. The children develop their confidence in a range of different musical experiences. All children take part in practical lessons within which they are given the opportunity to discover, explore and develop their technical skills.
Year R music
In Early Years, children are exposed to a range of songs, including nursery rhymes, in which they begin to develop an understanding of aspects such as beat and tune. To support with this they are encouraged to move to the music to express how it makes them feel. Children take part in a range of different listening activities and they are given time to explore a range of instruments noticing the different sounds that they make.
Year 1 and 2 music
Music is taught by a specialist Music teacher as a separate subject in KS1, although using cross-curricular links is encouraged. Within the weekly 30-minute specialist lessons, children are taught the musical learning for their level, including Beat, Pitch and Rhythm as well as using small percussion instruments. Children also are taught basic musical terms.
Within KS2, children are taught music through Music Express weekly as well as using aspects of cross curricular learning to support, including Computing. Children have their own music folder that holds evidence of their work as well as videos of their learning collated into a class shared area.
School Events
We believe that music enriches the lives of people, and so we endeavour to involve as many children as possible in musical activities. KS1 and KS2 take part in weekly worship, which involves developing skills linked to singing, including pitch and beat. Throughout the year, special Whole School Events are held, such as Harvest Festival, which allow the children to perform their music taught during Worship. Further whole school events are held to celebrate World Music Day in the Summer Term, where each year group gets a chance to showcase their learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary School - Nursery Admissions
pageCache.text:
Nursery Admissions
Nursery Admission Information
Thank you for looking at our nursery as an option for your child. We hope this information is of use and answers some of your questions.
We are a local church school and our nursery is open to children the term after their third birthday. Places are offered for five days a week, Monday to Friday, during school term-time. Our nursery starts at 8:45 am and finishes at 3:15. At this time, there is no breakfast club or afterschool club provision for nursery.
• Improve the on-entry levels of the children.
• To support our early intervention policy and provide support for our families.
The nursery has 26 places and we have three nursery intakes each academic year in September, January and April. If, after you have submitted an application form, we are able to offer your child a place we will contact you the term before they are due to start. Allocations will be awarded based on Rochester Riverside’s Admission Arrangements (SIF not applicable). Parents who do not receive an allocated place will be placed on a waiting list based upon these arrangements.
Please note; admission to FS1 (Nursery) is the responsibility of the school and is no guarantee of a place in our reception class (FS2) as Medway Council themselves are responsible for that admission process.
If you would like to apply for our nursery, a link to the application form can be found on our admissions page at www.rrcoe.medway.sch.uk. If you have any questions, please contact the school office on 01634 471697 or email admissions@rrcoe.medway.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary School - PTFA
pageCache.text:
PTFA
Who We Are
The Rochester Riverside Parent Teacher and Friends Association (PTFA) is a dedicated group of parents and carers who work in partnership with the school to enhance the educational experience of every child. As a registered charity, our purpose is to strengthen relationships between families, staff and the wider community, while raising funds and providing opportunities that enrich learning across the curriculum. We meet regularly, welcome all volunteers, and aim to build a warm, inclusive school community.
What We Do
Throughout the year, the PTFA organises a wide range of events—from bake sales and raffles to community meet‑ups and whole‑school celebrations. These activities not only raise valuable funds but also create memorable experiences for children and parents alike. We work closely with the senior leadership team to identify areas where additional resources or new opportunities will most benefit pupils. Alongside events, we actively pursue grants and community funding through partners such as the Co‑op, Tesco and Asda, ensuring the school can continue to offer high‑quality enrichment opportunities.
How We Support the School
Our fundraising directly benefits pupils across the school. In recent years, the PTFA has contributed to new sports, garden and kitchen equipment; library books and storage; classroom resources; and whole‑school experiences such as educational workshops and a visit from the gladiator “Steel”. We are committed to ensuring every child can access PTFA activities, offering a Pay‑It‑Forward scheme so that family circumstances never become a barrier to participation. In addition, our grant‑funded projects have helped develop outdoor learning environments including the kitchen garden and wellbeing garden, with further sustainability‑focused projects planned.

Transition
At Rochester Riverside Church of England Primary, we understand that change can feel big for families as your child moves through school life. Our approach to transition is designed to be calm, clear, and supportive: we share important information early, help children become familiar with routines and expectations, and provide opportunities to ask questions and build confidence. Staff work closely together to ensure continuity in learning and pastoral care, and we encourage parents to stay involved so that home and school are aligned. If you have any concerns, please speak with us—we are here to help your child feel safe, settled, and ready for the next step.

School Uniform
School Uniform
School sweatshirt or cardigan (Purple)
Polo Shirt (Gold / Mustard Yellow)
Grey trousers or skirt
Grey, black or white socks only
Grey fleece
During the summer:
Grey school shorts
Purple and white checked shorts
Purple and white checked summer dresses
Footwear
Black school shoes
No trainers
During the summer:
P.E. Kit
All children need to have the school P.E. kit which consists of:
Children taking part in outdoor games lessons must wear either trainers or plimsolls.
In gymnastics or dance in the hall, pupils are usually barefoot.
Earrings should be removed before school on your child’s P.E. day, no earrings are permitted during P.E.
School fleece or jumper
Grey polo shirt
Black shorts
Black tracksuit bottoms
Black plimsolls or black trainers
Hair / Earrings and Jewellery
Hairstyles should be reasonable and appropriate for being in a learning environment. Extreme hairstyles including shaved patterns in the scalp, mohicans and unnaturally coloured dyes are not acceptable. All children are required to have their hair tied back, if long enough.
Please note, only stud earrings are acceptable at school. Hoops and dropped earrings are not acceptable school uniform; if worn parents will be asked to come back into school and remove the earrings.
No other jewellery is permitted at school.
Ways to purchase your uniform
School Time are located at 87-89 High Street, Chatham, Kent, ME4 4HU. Orders can be placed either by visiting the shop. Items can be collected from the shop.
All items of school uniform, including footwear, must be marked with children's names.
